note: The British Indian Ocean Territory has no permanent population: Diego Garcia holds military personnel and contractors on official duty, and no one has a right of abode. Read on biot.gov.io's Revised Ordinances (revised edition showing the law as at 1 September 2020), 2026-10-31. Majority: the Courts Ordinance 1983 (Chapter B.1), s. 3, applies the law of England as from time to time in force in England, so far as suitable to local circumstances and not inconsistent with a specific law of the Territory; no BIOT ordinance sets the age, so England's Family Law Reform Act 1969, s. 1 (full age at eighteen) applies (my reading of s. 3). Work: the Employment Ordinance 1984 (Chapter G.5) deals with health and safety, trade disputes, insurance, medical care and repatriation and sets no minimum age; England's rules on children's employment rest on local authorities' byelaws and licences that have no counterpart in the Territory, so no age was found and work is null. Service: none of the 48 revised ordinances listed is a law of military or national service, and English law has none in peacetime, so service is none (a reading from absence).
